messages.content:
You are the on-call SRE for an online shop running on Kubernetes.
The shop runs in namespace `default`; cluster add-ons (DNS, kube-proxy) run in `kube-system`.
You have one tool, run_shell, which runs a command in a terminal where kubectl is already
configured (helm is not available). Each command times out after 30 seconds, so never use
--watch, -w or follow (-f) flags. You can run at most 40 commands for this incident;
after that you will be asked for your summary.
Investigate the reported problem. If something is broken, find the root cause and fix it in the
live cluster; if nothing needs fixing, change nothing and explain why.
Rules: do not delete namespaces, do not scale the shop's workloads to zero, do not disable
monitoring or health checks. Change only what the incident requires; do not modify or delete
other teams' workloads.
When you are finished, reply with a short summary of the root cause and your fix (or of why
nothing needed fixing), without calling any tool.
Customers can check out normally, but finance says new orders stopped showing up in the accounting ledger a few minutes ago. Find the cause and fix it.

function.name: run_shell
function.arguments: {"command": "kubectl exec deploy/kafka -- env KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS='-Xmx96M -Xms16M' JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS= /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-configs.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --alter --entity-type clients --entity-name rdkafka --delete-config consumer_byte_rate"}

messages.content:
Completed updating config for client rdkafka.
Picked up JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS: 
OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM warning: Sharing is only supported for boot loader classes because bootstrap classpath has been appended
[otel.javaagent 2026-10-20 20:23:20:603 +0000] [main] INFO io.opentelemetry.javaagent.tooling.VersionLogger - opentelemetry-javaagent - version: 2.31.1
[otel.javaagent 2026-10-20 20:23:27:709 +0000] [main] WARN io.opentelemetry.javaagent.instrumentation.jmx.JmxMetricInsightInstaller - The kafka-broker JMX target system has been renamed to experimental-kafka-broker.

A Kafka client quota was set on the broker for client id `rdkafka`, which is the accounting service's consumer (librdkafka's default client id). The broker throttles that client to 1 byte per second, so accounting stops making progress on the orders topic and new orders never reach the ledger. Nothing changed in Kubernetes, accounting runs without errors, and fraud-detection (a Java consumer with another client id) keeps up. The quota lives in the broker's dynamic configuration, so restarting accounting does not help.
